name: Dark Violet
lede: Dark Violet is a web color, `darkviolet`, a vivid purple defined by the hex code 9400D3 in the X11 color set.

sections.title: A web color
sections.body:
Paterson lists DarkViolet among the colors of the X11 color set, with the hex code 9400D3 [1]. It is a standard label, a place on a computer chart, not a historical pigment name [1].

The swatch is a saturated purple, more electric than [[purple]] and more red than [[blue-violet]], with [[dark-orchid]] as its nearest neighbor in the same list [1]. Screen colors are approximate.

sections.title: Dark violet in older books
sections.body:
The phrase dark violet turns up in older color writing as plain description. Gage cites a medieval treatise complaining that painters and illuminators did not know what color to use for heraldic purple; one choice was the color of mulberries, which the author calls a dark violet [2]. Heraldry is where the idea of a single royal purple finally broke down [2].

Birren summarizes an old color-therapy scheme that paired yellow-green with dark violet as complements [3]. Gage adds that early writers set dark violet against green [4]. Complements depend on the system used, so no one pairing is true everywhere [3][4]. In pigment books, the Pigment Compendium notes that heating chromate of stannic oxide gives a dark violet mass, tin violet, which Salter in 1869 judged better for enamel than for the palette [5].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our archive of 23,781 has this color covering at least 1 per cent of its canvas, within CIEDE2000 4 of it [6]. That describes our archive, as photographed, and not painting as a whole [6]. The phrase *dark violet* peaks in Google Books at roughly 1870 on a rough reading [6].
